items.title: Allen Toussaint Interview, 1979-03-13
items.q: INTERVIEWER: ...simply entitled Two Saints, with Mack Rebinack and Earl Turbington... [INTERVIEWEE] I remember it. ... I remember doing it

ctx.x: I don't know. Don't really know.

You recorded a second album, which I like a lot. I hope you feel good about it. It was on Tiffany Records, simply entitled Two Saints, with Mack Rebinack and Earl Turbington, to name but a few. And that was recently released on an English label, I think two years ago, and it finally came back to New Orleans. And we played it, playing it tremendously on WTUL this last summer. Do you have good feelings about that album? It has working on a coal mine on it and a lot of beautiful instrumental work.

I remember it. And that's the way it is. I remember it. I never hear it anymore, of course. I remember doing it and it felt very different from that much singing going on for the first time. On the earlier album, it was all instrumental. So I could hold on to the piano. But to sing, sing your spirit through a microphone. Steve Terrell, that was with Scepter and Juan Records, talked up that album. And I consented to do that, but I'd never tried that before.
